title: CtrlAltBen Frontier Model Tracker catalogue observation
comment: One file is one run of one source in one region that saw at least one change. A run that sees nothing new writes no file; the chain of files attests those silent runs through previous_run_at, runs_since_previous_file and keys_present. See docs/catalogue-contract.md.

source.comment: The listing the run read. The v1 value is arm (the Azure Resource Manager Models API); the vocabulary is open so another listing can be added without a new schema version.

region.comment: The ARM lowercase region identifier, for example uksouth.

observed_at.comment: The run that saw the changes. An observation dates the observation, never the change itself.

previous_run_at.comment: The last successful run of the same source and region. It is the 'absent at' edge of every first-seen window in the file.

runs_since_previous_file.comment: Silent successful runs between the previous file and this one, none of which saw a change.

previous_file.comment: Path, relative to the repository root, of the previous observation file for this source and region, or null for the first file after a checkpoint with no earlier file.

checkpoint.comment: Path of the latest checkpoint at or before this file. Required and not nullable: a diff file never exists without a seed checkpoint.

observed_from.comment: The literal label for the vantage point of the run, for example 'standard pay-as-you-go subscription'. A listing is one subscription's view, which is why absence is weaker evidence than presence.

entry_count.comment: Model entries the run saw in total, not the number that changed.

cell_count.comment: Deployment-type cells the run saw in total, not the number that changed.

snapshot_sha256.comment: SHA-256 of the full normalised snapshot the watcher holds privately, so a replay can show it reached the same state without the snapshot being published.

keys_present.comment: The full list of model keys the run saw, not only the changed ones. A key absent here but present in the replayed state is an absence the run saw.

model_key.comment: name@version exactly as the API spells them, case preserved, for example gpt-chat-latest@2026-10-07 or Muse-Glimmer-30B@1. The version is a build identifier, never a date.

window_start.comment: The run at which the old state was last seen. Every change is a window from one run to the next, never a day.

window_end.comment: The run at which the new state was first seen. For last_seen_absent this is the first absent run, and confirmed_at says when the absence was confirmed.

confirmed_at.comment: Absences only: the run at which the absence was confirmed.

absence_strength.comment: Absences only. The listing is one subscription's view, so ARM absences are always weak; page is reserved for a source that publishes the listing itself.

fields.comment: The watched field names that changed.

before.comment: The watched subset before the change: present on changes and absences.

after.comment: The watched subset after the change: present on arrivals and changes.

note.comment: Free text, for example: Legacy is mapped to the portal's Legacy stage; the REST enum omits it.

watched.comment: The watched subset of a model entry. systemData timestamps are never watched and never appear here.

lifecycle_status.comment: The raw API value, shown beside its portal word from schema/lifecycle-mapping.json.

lifecycle_portal.comment: The portal word for lifecycle_status from schema/lifecycle-mapping.json; null when the value is unmapped.

cell.comment: One deployment type of one model entry in the region. Capacity is a moment, read at capacity_at, not a standing quantity.

deployment_type.comment: The ARM skuName, or none when the row carries skus: [].

capacity.comment: Absent, not zero, when capacity was not read.
